headline: Weekend Brief: US stock futures rose as oil fell on Iran de-escalation hopes and yen support efforts ahead of key ISM and JOLTS data
raw_text:
- US stock futures traded higher as crude oil (@CL) prices declined on optimism around a pause in Iran-related fighting, potential Hormuz Strait deal progress, and reduced geopolitical risk.
- The sharp drop in crude put downward pressure on US energy stocks in premarket indications, while broader indices and financials were poised to benefit from an improved risk-on tone.
- Reports of joint US–Japan yen (@6J) intervention efforts and earlier signals of yen (@6J) support bolstered risk sentiment and supported exporter-linked names.
- Banks were reported to be hedging leveraged ETF exposures with crash puts, signaling ongoing concern about downside risk despite a firmer tone in equities.
- Speculation emerged around a possible AstraZeneca (AZN)–Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) merger, raising potential implications for valuations across the broader pharma sector.
- Prysmian was reportedly nearing a takeover of US electrical equipment maker Atkore (ATKR), underscoring renewed M&A interest in industrials.
- Traders focused on Monday’s US macro releases, including July ISM Manufacturing PMI, S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, and Construction Spending data.
- The June JOLTS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey at 10:00 AM ET was in focus as a key labor-market indicator ahead of this week’s nonfarm payrolls report.
- Market participants also watched for earnings and guidance updates from Marriott (MAR), Palantir (PLTR), Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX), Williams Companies, ONEOK (OKE), and Diamondback Energy (FANG) before and after the US cash session.
